FICTIONAL SAMPLE - NOT A REAL PATIENT
Riverside General Hospital - Discharge Instructions
Patient: Harbans Kaur        Age: 74
Discharge date: October 22, 2026
Reason for stay: Fast heart rhythm (atrial fibrillation) and fluid in the lungs

DISCHARGE MEDICATION LIST
Please follow this list. It replaces any list you had before.

NEW medications (start taking):
- Metoprolol tartrate 25 mg - take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily with food.
- Apixaban 5 mg - take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily, about 12 hours apart. Do not skip doses.
- Furosemide 20 mg - take 1 tablet by mouth once daily in the morning for 5 days, then stop.

CHANGED medications:
- Atorvastatin - dose increased. Now take 40 mg (1 tablet) by mouth once daily at bedtime.

CONTINUE taking as before:
- Metformin 500 mg - take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily with breakfast and dinner.
- Acetaminophen 500 mg - take 1 to 2 tablets by mouth every 6 hours as needed for pain. Do not take more than 6 tablets in 24 hours.

STOP taking these medications:
- Amlodipine 5 mg - STOP. Your blood pressure is now treated with metoprolol.
- Aspirin 81 mg - STOP. Apixaban replaces aspirin. Taking both increases bleeding risk.

FOLLOW-UP
- See Dr. Okafor (cardiology) in 1 week. The clinic will call to book.
- Blood test for kidney function and potassium in 5 days.

WHEN TO GET HELP
Call your doctor or go to emergency if you have:
- Chest pain, or a heartbeat that feels very fast or irregular
- Black or bloody stools, or bleeding that will not stop
- Swelling in the legs or weight gain of more than 2 kg in 2 days
- Feeling dizzy or faint

FICTIONAL SAMPLE BOTTLE LABEL (photographed in the family kitchen)
Extra Strength TYLENOL
Acetaminophen 500 mg caplets
Directions: adults take 2 caplets every 6 hours while symptoms last. Do not take more than 6 caplets in 24 hours.
